questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A book lying on a table pushes down on the table and the table pushes up on the book. These two forces:
options: Are an action-reaction pair acting on different bodies
Act on the same body and balance each other
Add up to give the net force on the book
questions.explanation: Action and reaction never act on the same body, so they can never cancel each other. The book stays at rest because its weight is balanced by the normal reaction from the table.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two electric field lines can never intersect each other because:
options: At the point of intersection the field would have two directions, which is impossible
questions.explanation: The tangent to a field line gives the direction of the field at that point, and a field can have only one direction at a point. Field lines also never form closed loops in electrostatics.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 1: Electric Charges and Fields

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The Davisson and Germer experiment, in which electrons were scattered from a nickel crystal, provided direct evidence for:
options: The wave nature of electrons, as predicted by de Broglie
questions.explanation: The electrons produced a diffraction pattern, something only waves can do, and the measured wavelength matched h/mv exactly.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 11: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The mass of carbon dioxide obtained by completely decomposing 50 g of calcium carbonate (molar mass 100 g/mol) is:
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ gives CaO and CO₂ in a 1 : 1 mole ratio. 50/100 = 0.5 mol of CaCO₃ gives 0.5 mol of CO₂, which weighs 0.5 × 44 = 22 g.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the conformations of ethane, the staggered form is more stable than the eclipsed form because:
options: The hydrogen atoms are farthest apart, so torsional strain is minimum
It has a higher molecular mass
questions.explanation: The energy difference is only about 12.5 kJ per mole, so at room temperature rotation about the C-C bond is nearly free and the conformers cannot be isolated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of acidic strength is:
questions.explanation: The carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance over two equivalent oxygens, the phenoxide ion over the ring alone, and the ethoxide ion not at all.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: According to the chemiosmotic hypothesis, ATP synthesis in the chloroplast is driven by:
options: A proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane
Direct transfer of phosphate from NADPH
Absorption of CO₂ in the stroma
questions.explanation: Protons accumulate in the thylakoid lumen and then flow out through the F₀ channel of ATP synthase, and that flow drives the enzyme to make ATP.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The four major causes of biodiversity loss, called the evil quartet, include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The evil quartet is habitat loss and fragmentation, over exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction. In-situ conservation is a remedy, not a cause.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The respiratory rhythm centre that primarily regulates breathing in humans is located in the:
questions.explanation: A pneumotaxic centre in the pons can moderate this centre, and rising CO₂ and H⁺ in the blood are the main stimuli that increase the rate of breathing.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In sickle cell anaemia, the substitution of valine for glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta globin chain results from a change in:
options: A single base pair in the gene, that is a point mutation
The loss of an entire chromosome
A deletion of the whole gene
questions.explanation: GAG becomes GUG, and that one change makes the haemoglobin crystallise into a sickle shape under low oxygen. The heterozygote is protected against malaria.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
